node.title: The negation-closure excess and its razor kill
node.closure: exact structural excess family with a rho-threshold fence
node.statement: On a negation-closed evaluation domain D = {+-1,...,+-m} (n = 2m), which the official power-of-two multiplicative subgroup is, column-far razor-faithful pencils with e_1 = x^2 e_0 carry T = 95..98 bad slopes against r+1 = 9, field-size independently and at mu_1 down to 1.26e-7, beating the first moment by 750x with zero saturation; the same family on the non-closed domain {1,...,20} gives T = 10. The mechanism is exact: since v_{-x} = (-1)^{n-1} v_x and sum_x v_x g(x) = 0 for deg g <= n-2, an even locator sigma(x) = Q(x^2) with root set A u (-A) collapses every odd-index Hankel row onto the orbits the error support misses, so a locator covering those orbits leaves exactly ceil(rho/2) conditions on the single unknown slope. Hence rho = 2 yields one slope per covering even locator and rho >= 3 yields generically none. The number of covering even locators is C(m-off, r/2-off) with off = m-(r+1); the banked form C(m-1, r/2-1) is its off = 1 face. At rho = 2 the bad set equals the covering set exactly (84 at H1, 330 at H3, both fields), though at H3 those 330 locators carry only 329 distinct slopes. The excess is killed at the razor exactly: ceil(rho/M) = 1 needs M >= rho = 2^34, and at M = 2 the surplus is 2^33 - 1 = 8589934591 conditions -- a rho-threshold, not a field threshold. Consequently any far-CA counting argument treating D as a generic point set is unsound at small rho.
